newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 18.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 18.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Wednesday and main factors likely to affect trading:

* Trendless trading and timid volumes will characterise the market as investors await release of second quarter corporate results which are seen as mixed, said BPI Securities Corp analyst Spencer Yap.
* Sun Hung Kai Securities Phil Inc said trading will be passive in the next few days as market players are sidelined by talk of unfavourable second quarter earnings results.
* On Tuesday, the Philippine composite index closed 7.39 points higher at 2,798.26.
* The Dow Jones on Tuesday ended 11.31 points lower at 7,760.78. PLDT's ADR closed $1 3/4 higher at $63 3/4.
* The Philippine peso closed higher at 26.375 to the dollar vs 26.377.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was steady at 13.03125 percent.
* The yield on the Philippine five-year treasury note rose to 13 percent from the previous 12.5 percent, the Bureau of Treasury said on Tuesday.
* The Central Bank said the Salomon Brothers had been named the firm underwriter out of five banks bidding for the position. Salomon has begun offering the bonds.
* The Central Bank said it would save money on its revamped yankee bond issue and hoped to have its side of the deal wrapped up by the end of the month.

* Tight pricing offered for the maiden yankee bond issue of the Central Bank has turned off several potential buyers, senior bankers and bond traders said. The 30-year bonds are being offered at 185 basis points above the U.S. long bond, while the 100-year bond is 197.5 bp over.
* ING Barings said it would syndicate a $150 million loan for oil refiner Petron Corp.
* The Philippines' trade deficit dropped 34.8 percent to $860 million in April compared with the year-ago $1.319 billion, the National Statistics Office (NSO) said.
* The NSO said total trade deficit in the first four months of the year totalled $3.753 billion, down 5.9 percent compared with $3.99 billion in the same period last year.
* PICOP Resources Inc said it expected a financial turnaround next year because of the general elections in May.

* The newspaper Business Daily said the Securities and Exchange Commission will conduct another in-depth investigation into the case of four brokers accused of price manipulation. An initial but "inconclusive" report of the SEC prosecution and enforcement department point to a probable conspiracy.
* But BusinessWorld said SEC officials deny the existence of a report that allegedly found foreign stock brokerage firms conspiring to manipulate prices.
